title: Dual MDM2 and PPARG regulatory axes mediate the antiepileptic effects of Gouteng: An integration of bioinformatics, network pharmacology, machine learning, molecular docking, and MD simulations.
authors: Zhang, Hong-Quan; Chen, Lin; Yuan, Xian-Jun; Luo, Yao-Xue; Duan, Li-Xin; Lin, Ya-Qi; Wang, Rui-Ge
one_liner_zh: 该文整合网络药理学、机器学习、分子对接和MD模拟研究钩藤抗癫痫机制，虽涉及蛋白-小分子对接及TFAP2C转录因子，但核心对象为药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，仅边缘相关。
abstract: Gouteng is a traditional Chinese medicine widely used for the clinical treatment of epilepsy, yet the specific mechanism underlying its antiepileptic has not been elucidated. Network pharmacology, bioinformatics, machine learning, molecular docking, MD simulation, and ADMET druggability analysis were performed to systematically elucidate the molecular regulatory mechanism of Gouteng against epilepsy. The results showed that 29 active components of Gouteng collectively regulated 661 potential antiepileptic targets. Through screening with machine learning-based disease diagnostic model, MDM2 and PPARG as the core target genes mediating the antiepileptic effect of Gouteng were finally identified. Immune infiltration analysis confirmed that MDM2 and PPARG synergistically reshape the immune microenvironment of epileptic lesions, restrain excessive inflammatory responses, and maintain immune homeostasis and tolerance. Molecular docking and MD simulation revealed that the four core active components, namely Angustidine, Rhynchophylline A, vincoside lactam_qt, and coryincine, target the hydrophobic pocket of MDM2, with non-polar interactions serving as the primary driving factor for their interactions. ADMET analysis indicated that vincoside lactam_qt and coryincine exhibit favorable oral bioavailability, excellent blood-brain barrier permeability, and low hepatotoxicity, which make them potential antiepileptic candidate drugs with clinical translational potential. Most importantly, Gouteng exerts antiepileptic effects by targeting and regulating the dual MDM2-MDM4/TP53 and PPARG-NCOA1/RXRA regulatory axes, thereby mediating neuroinflammation inhibition and neuronal protection. Furthermore, TFAP2C as a common upstream transcription factor of both MDM2 and PPARG was identified. This study provides theoretical basis for the development of novel MDM2/PPARG-targeted antiepileptic drugs and for the clinical application of Gouteng.
abstract_zh: 钩藤是一种广泛应用于临床治疗癫痫的传统中药，但其抗癫痫的具体机制尚未阐明。本研究采用网络药理学、生物信息学、机器学习、分子对接、分子动力学（MD）模拟及ADMET成药性分析，系统阐明钩藤抗癫痫的分子调控机制。结果显示，钩藤的29种活性成分共同调控661个潜在抗癫痫靶点。通过基于机器学习的疾病诊断模型筛选，最终确定MDM2和PPARG为介导钩藤抗癫痫作用的核心靶基因。免疫浸润分析证实，MDM2和PPARG协同重塑癫痫病灶的免疫微环境，抑制过度炎症反应，并维持免疫稳态和耐受性。分子对接和MD模拟揭示，四种核心活性成分，即Angustidine、Rhynchophylline A、vincoside lactam_qt和coryincine，靶向MDM2的疏水口袋，其中非极性相互作用是其相互作用的主要驱动力。ADMET分析表明，vincoside lactam_qt和coryincine具有良好的口服生物利用度、优异的血脑屏障通透性和低肝毒性，使其成为具有临床转化潜力的潜在抗癫痫候选药物。最重要的是，钩藤通过靶向调控MDM2-MDM4/TP53和PPARG-NCOA1/RXRA双重调控轴发挥抗癫痫作用，从而介导神经炎症抑制和神经元保护。此外，TFAP2C被鉴定为MDM2和PPARG的共同上游转录因子。本研究为开发新型靶向MDM2/PPARG的抗癫痫药物及钩藤的临床应用提供了理论基础。
